# Gym recharge-time tuning sliders (dedicated tuning gym)

## Problem statement

Phase Shift and Teleport now recharge per charge, but their recharge times are
level-derived only (`phaseRechargeRate` 30 s → 10 s, `teleportRechargeRate`
60 s → 20 s). A balance observer cannot answer "what if Teleport recharged in
8 s?" without editing the level catalogue and reloading. There is no place to
watch the two defensive abilities cycle under sustained threat while varying
their recharge times.

## Users

- **Balance tuner (primary):** needs a dedicated gym where Phase Shift and
  Teleport are permanently owned from the first frame and attacked from more
  than one direction, with live sliders for each recharge time — so recharge
  pacing can be judged by eye and the chosen value persisted for the next
  session.
- **Producer / designer (secondary):** needs the tuning knobs to stay
  gym-only, so shipped gameplay defaults are never changed by accident.

Example user stories:

- *As a balance tuner, I want a gym that starts me with Phase Shift and
  Teleport already owned, so I do not have to farm drops before observing a
  recharge cycle.*
- *As a balance tuner, I want two groups of shooting enemies so both
  defensive abilities are triggered repeatedly from different directions.*
- *As a balance tuner, I want to drag a "Phase Shift recharge" slider and see
  the next spent charge return in the new time, and have that value survive a
  page reload.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new dedicated gym scene `GymRechargeTuning` (`src/scenes/gym/GymRechargeTuning.ts`) spawns the player at screen centre with **Phase Shift and Teleport granted as permanent power-ups from the first frame** (each a recharging charge pool, cap 3), so both abilities auto-activate under threat without collecting a drop.
- The gym spawns **at least two groups of shooting `raider` enemies** (default 3 per group, placed left and right of the player) with shooting enabled by default, plus an in-panel SHOOT toggle and the shared wave-timeout refresh, so threat pressure is sustained.
- Two live sliders ("Phase Shift recharge" and "Teleport recharge") live in a plain-DOM `.gym-panel`, reuse the `buildSpawnIntervalSlider` pattern, cover **Phase 1–60 s / Teleport 1–120 s at 0.5 s steps**, display **seconds**, and **immediately change the recharge time applied to subsequently spent charges**.
- Slider values **persist via the rules config** as `phaseRechargeOverrideSeconds` / `teleportRechargeOverrideSeconds` (`number | null`; `null`/absent = level-derived default) and are re-applied on scene create; the gym seeds each slider from the persisted override or the level-derived default when unset.
- The override is **gym-only**: the shipped `PlayScene` and every other gym keep level-derived recharge times (the override is read by the tuning gym, not applied to gameplay defaults).
- Unit tests cover the slider DOM (ids, labels, min/max/step, output), live application to the recharge timers, the rules persistence round-trip, the `null` fallback, and the two-group enemy spawn with shooting on — in `src/scenes/gym/GymRechargeTuning.test.ts`.
- A `GymRechargeTuning` row is added to `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` recording its enabled objects, spawn seam and any retained divergence (guarded by `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts`).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym ↔ game parity:** the new gym must consume the shared seams — `createEnemyFromConfig` + `resolveSpawnTransitTarget` for spawning, the shared wave timeout, `CombatScene`/`CombatCoreScene` helpers — not a divergent copy (AGENTS.md Game Architecture Conventions).
- **Reuse the slider pattern:** extend `src/utils/gymPowerUpControl.ts` with a recharge slider builder and persist helper rather than duplicating the DOM code.
- **Do not change shipped defaults:** the level catalogue's recharge rates stay authoritative for gameplay; the override is an optional gym/rules layer.
- **Backward-compatible rules blob:** new optional fields coerce to `null` when absent; existing saved rules must still load.
- **Run-scoped timers:** the override applies to timer durations set at consumption; in-flight timers are not retro-fitted (matching the run-scoped recharge model).
- **Auto-discovery:** `GymIndex` discovers `Gym*.ts` automatically, so no index registration edit is needed — but the parity row is still mandatory.

## Existing state

- **Recharge model:** `PowerUpLevelStore` (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`) tracks per-charge recharge timers; `phaseRechargeTime()` / `teleportRechargeTime()` derive seconds from the level axes (`phaseRechargeRate` 1/30 → 1/10 charges/s; `teleportRechargeRate` 1/60 → 1/20 charges/s); `EffectsRegistry.tick` advances `tickRecharge(dt)`.
- **No override mechanism:** recharge time is level-derived only; there is no rules-level or store-level override.
- **Slider precedent:** `src/utils/gymPowerUpControl.ts` exports `buildSpawnIntervalSlider(onApply)` and `applyAndPersistSpawnInterval(seconds)`; used by `GymBoss` and `GymFodderEnemies`.
- **Permanent grants:** `grantPermanentPowerUp(id, effectsRegistry)` → `effectsRegistry.applyCollect(id, true)` (`src/powerups/choiceReward.ts`).
- **Reference scene shape:** `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` (player + 3-scout V-formation, SHOOT toggle, wave timeout, shared `CombatScene`).

## Desired change

- Add an optional recharge-time override seam to `PowerUpLevelStore` (e.g. `setRechargeTimeOverride(phaseSeconds | null, teleportSeconds | null)`) honoured by `phaseRechargeTime()` / `teleportRechargeTime()`, falling back to the level-derived value when unset.
- Add optional `phaseRechargeOverrideSeconds` / `teleportRechargeOverrideSeconds` (`number | null`) to `GameRules`, its defaults and `loadRules` coercion.
- Add `buildRechargeTimeSlider(...)` and a persist helper to `src/utils/gymPowerUpControl.ts`.
- Create the `GymRechargeTuning` scene: player + permanent Phase Shift/Teleport grants, two `raider` groups with SHOOT on, panel with the two recharge sliders wired to the store override and rules persistence.
- Add tests, the parity row and the documentation note.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymRechargeTuning.ts` — New scene: player, permanent grants, two raider groups, tuning panel.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymRechargeTuning.test.ts` — Slider DOM, live application, persistence, fallback and spawn tests.
- `src/utils/gymPowerUpControl.ts` — Add a recharge-time slider builder + persist helper.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — Recharge-time override seam on `PowerUpLevelStore`.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — Optional override fields, defaults and load coercion.
- `src/core/rules.test.ts` — Persistence/coercion tests for the new fields.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — Add the `GymRechargeTuning` parity row.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Note the gym-only tuning control if the levelling section describes recharge.

## Related work

- AH-0MV2N0FX2004KEPR — Teleport and Phase Shift should recharge (parent/recharge model).
- AH-0MW231MCL000MMUU — Store readiness: spending Teleport starts the timer.
- AH-0MVY096RT006QMF4 — Teleport regenerates too quickly.
- AH-0MV82IA9U004BOKP — HUD recharge countdown indicator (sibling follow-up).
- AH-0MV82IAM7004KOYQ — Recharge-complete audio cue (sibling follow-up).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — Gym ↔ game parity convention.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What is being tuned — which abilities and which property?" — Answer (producer): "Phase Shift and Teleport recharge times." Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).
- Q: "Which gym scene(s) should get the recharge sliders?" — Answer (producer): "Create a Gym specifically for tuning these. It should spawn a player who has them as permanent power-ups from the start. There should be at least two groups of shooting enemies." Final: a new dedicated `GymRechargeTuning` scene. Source: interactive reply (intake round 2).
- Q: "How should the sliders override recharge — absolute time, a multiplier, or both?" — Answer (producer): "1. A". Final: (A) absolute recharge time in seconds, applied as an override on the level-derived value. Source: interactive reply (intake round 3).
- Q: "What should the two enemy groups be?" — Answer (producer): "2. B you choose". Final: two groups of `raider` archetype (3 per group, left and right), chosen for mobile aimed fire that creates converging, sustained pressure; `EnemyConfig` remains the retuning surface. Source: interactive reply (intake round 3).
- Q: "Slider count, range, display and persistence?" — Answer: implied acceptance of the stated defaults (two sliders; Phase 1–60 s / Teleport 1–120 s at 0.5 s steps; display seconds; persist via rules with `null` = level-derived), since the producer answered only the two explicit questions and did not object to the defaults. Source: interactive reply (intake round 3); recorded as an assumption for producer confirmation at plan/review.


## Impact

A balance tuner can open a dedicated gym where Phase Shift and Teleport are already owned and under sustained raider fire, drag a slider to change either recharge time and watch the next spent charge come back in the new time, with the chosen value surviving a page reload while shipped gameplay keeps its level-derived defaults.

## Implementation notes & assumptions

- **Teleport `cap 3` wording.** The work item's AC parenthetical says both abilities are "a recharging charge pool, cap 3". Phase Shift is a pooled consumable whose regenerating ceiling is 3 and is honoured exactly. Teleport is **single-use** in the shipped recharge model (parent AH-0MVY096RT006QMF4): its whole state is one readiness timer (cap 1). Giving it a stored multi-charge pool would change shipped gameplay, which this gym must not do, so the gym grants Teleport permanently (leaving its single warp ready) and exposes its level-derived recharge time through the same slider/override seam. Recorded as a reasonable assumption for producer confirmation at review.
- **Gym-only override.** `PowerUpLevelStore.setRechargeTimeOverride(phaseSeconds, teleportSeconds)` is read only by the tuning gym; `GameRules.phaseRechargeOverrideSeconds` / `teleportRechargeOverrideSeconds` default to `null` (level-derived) and coerce absent/corrupt values to `null`, so existing rules blobs are backward-compatible. `PlayScene` and every other gym never read the override.
- **Run-scoped timers.** The override is resolved when a charge is spent, so it applies to subsequently spent charges; an in-flight timer keeps the duration captured at spend time (covered by tests).
- **Auto-discovery + registries.** The scene is discovered automatically by `GymIndex`; the capture registry (`scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`), `examples/scenes.json`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, the parity guard's scene list and the GymIndex ordering test were updated to match.
- **Test evidence.** Full suite green at the implementation commit: 10,549 tests passed (467 files). Changed-scope gate covers `GymRechargeTuning.test.ts`, `rules.test.ts`, `powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `gymParityDocs.test.ts` and `capture-scenes.test.ts`.

## Goal

Crash resilience for dev telemetry: stream each flushed telemetry batch to the
dev server **during the run** so that a page reload/crash mid-run loses at most
one in-flight batch instead of the whole run's un-uploaded tail.

Today the dev JSONL sink is an in-memory, per-run buffer
(`createMemoryLineWriter()`, AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3) that is POSTed **once at run
end** (`uploadDevTelemetry`). A crash or reload before that POST loses the
entire run; streaming bounds the loss to the batch in flight (~64 records,
~1.3 s of play at default settings) and removes the page-reload regression that
the old localStorage-backed sink accidentally masked.

This item is the explicitly deferred follow-up to the in-memory-sink work
(`discovered-from:AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3`); it was parked until that item landed
(it shipped in v0.1.15) and must not be implemented concurrently with it in the
same worktree.

## Problem statement

The dev telemetry pipeline buffers records in memory, flushes them in batches of
`DEFAULT_TELEMETRY_BATCH_SIZE` (64) into the per-run in-memory sink, and only
uploads the whole buffer at run end from `PlayScene._finishRun()` →
`flushAndUploadDevTelemetry()`. Browser memory is volatile: a page reload or
renderer crash between the last flush and the run-end POST discards the entire
run. The old localStorage sink survived a reload (until the quota filled), so
moving to memory introduced a detectable regression for interrupted runs.

The production sink is **not** affected: `HttpTelemetryTransport` already
streams each recorded batch to the configured remote endpoint with retry and
backoff. Only the dev (`jsonl`) path uploads at run end.

## Users

- **Developer / operator running a dev session** — "As a developer playing or
  recording a dev run, when the page reloads or crashes mid-run, I want the dev
  server to already have all but the last second or so of telemetry, so a long
  session is not lost and I do not have to reproduce it."
- **Developer running the dev CLI tooling** — "As a developer, I want
  `npm run record`, `npm run capture` and `npm run verify-dev-telemetry` to
  keep working exactly as they do, reading the full run from the page buffer at
  run end, so streaming does not break my existing workflow."
- **Maintainer of the dev telemetry server** — "As a maintainer, I want the dev
  server to store each run's records exactly once in one session file and to
  run the automatic evaluation once per run, so partial and final uploads
  cannot double-count or trigger duplicate evaluations."

## Existing state (verified in code)

- `src/telemetry/sinks.ts` — `createMemoryLineWriter()` is the `jsonl` sink's
  default line writer: an unbounded in-memory `string[]` with `read()`/`reset()`.
  `JsonlTelemetrySink.write()` serialises a batch to lines and appends them;
  `read()` returns the whole buffer as NDJSON, `reset()` clears it.
- `src/telemetry/recorder.ts` — `BufferedTelemetryRecorder` drains a 512-record
  ring buffer into batches of `batchSize` (64) and hands them to the sink on a
  serialised `writeChain`. `startRun()` clears the ring buffer and resets the
  sink, so a run's recording is run-scoped.
- `src/telemetry/devUpload.ts` — `uploadDevTelemetry()` reads the whole buffer
  through the injected `readSink` seam and POSTs it once at run end to
  `POST /api/telemetry/upload` (NDJSON, same-origin), fire-and-forget, with an
  8 MiB CDP-message cap (`DEFAULT_MAX_DEV_UPLOAD_MESSAGE_BYTES`, ceiling 16 MiB;
  over-cap bodies are skipped with one actionable line). The buffer is left
  intact after a successful upload.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_initTelemetry()` installs the dev-gated
  `window.__aiHellTelemetry = { read() }` accessor (returning the whole run
  buffer) and calls `startRun`; `_finishRun()` calls
  `flushAndUploadDevTelemetry()`, which flushes the recorder and then uploads the
  whole buffer.
- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` — the `POST /api/telemetry/upload`
  middleware validates the body with `parseRecording()`, stores it as one
  `recordings/session-<stamp>.jsonl` (collision-safe), and enqueues **one**
  background evaluation per upload. `apply: 'serve'` only; the endpoint is
  absent from a production bundle (bundle-hygiene marker).
- Dev CLI tooling — `scripts/record-session.mjs` and
  `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` read the run at run end through
  `window.__aiHellTelemetry` (chunked, bounded reads);
  `scripts/verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` plays a run, then asserts a new
  `recordings/session-*.jsonl`, ≥1 `POST /api/telemetry/upload` all 200, one
  `eval-output/uploaded/<stamp>/` with `human-balance-report.json`, a non-empty
  page buffer, and zero uploads/recordings when the share setting is off.
- Pinned contract — `src/telemetry/devUpload.test.ts` pins "buffer content left
  intact after a successful upload"; `verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` pins
  `session-*.jsonl` naming and one evaluation per run.

## Desired change

**Recommended design: a per-batch part protocol on the existing endpoint**
(option 1 of the item's proposed design), rather than a heartbeat/checkpoint
(option 2). Option 1 streams every flushed batch, so the ≤1-batch bound holds
without a separate recovery-on-demand flow; a heartbeat still needs a reload
recovery path and cannot beat option 1's bound unless it, too, fires per batch.

### Client (game)

1. **Observe every flushed batch.** Add a dev-only post-flush observer to the
   dev JSONL sink (e.g. an optional `onFlush(deltaNdjson)` callback in
   `TelemetrySinkDeps`/`JsonlTelemetrySink`) invoked after a batch is appended,
   carrying only that batch's NDJSON lines. The sink buffer is **never cleared
   mid-run** — only an upload watermark advances.
2. **Stream parts in order.** A dev-only streamer (`src/telemetry/devStream.ts`,
   loaded through the `devMode` gate like `loadDevTelemetryUploader`) POSTs each
   delta one at a time (serialised chain), with `runKey` (generated at
   `startRun` from `startedAt`+`runSeed`, e.g. `<startedAt>-<runSeed>`),
   `offset` (cumulative record count already confirmed by the server) and a
   `final` flag on the last part.
3. **Exactly-once by server-authoritative offset.** The streamer advances its
   watermark only when the server confirms the new cumulative appended count.
   A part whose 2xx was lost is re-sent from the last confirmed offset and the
   server drops the already-appended prefix; a gap (`offset` beyond the
   server's count) is rejected so the client re-syncs. Parts are serialised so
   records never interleave out of order.
4. **Offline/unreachable.** A failed part does not advance the watermark; the
   unconfirmed delta stays in the (never-cleared) in-memory buffer and is
   retried — with light bounded backoff to avoid hammering a down server. At
   run end the final part carries whatever remains beyond the confirmed offset,
   so an outage degrades to today's single run-end upload (still subject to the
   8 MiB CDP cap).
5. **Run end.** `flushAndUploadDevTelemetry()` flushes the recorder, sends the
   final part (`final: true`) and the server finalises the run's session file and
   enqueues exactly one evaluation. `window.__aiHellTelemetry.read()` continues
   to return the full run after run end (unchanged CLI behaviour).

### Server (dev only)

1. **Part protocol on the same path.** Discriminate parts with an explicit
   marker (header or query flag) on `POST /api/telemetry/upload` so
   `verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` (which matches that path) observes them and the
   bundle-hygiene marker stays valid. Without the marker, the existing
   whole-file behaviour is unchanged (store `session-<stamp>.jsonl`, evaluate
   once) — preserving the current contract and the production-preview test.
2. **Stage parts off the `session-*.jsonl` glob.** Append part records to
   `recordings/parts/<runKey>.jsonl` (outside the `session-*.jsonl` pattern, so a
   mid-run session is never mistaken for a completed recording by
   `verify-dev-telemetry` or `recordings()` helpers). Append only records beyond
   the stored count (dedupe by offset); reject a gap with the current count.
3. **Finalise once.** On `final: true`, rename the staged file to the existing
   collision-safe `recordings/session-<stamp>.jsonl` name and enqueue **one**
   evaluation (existing `EvaluationQueue`). Return 200 JSON with the merged
   record count.
4. **Crashed runs.** A run that never sends a final part leaves only
   `recordings/parts/<runKey>.jsonl` — valid NDJSON, readable by
   `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` and evaluable with `evaluate.mjs --human`, but
   not auto-evaluated (evaluation belongs to complete runs). Partial cleanup is
   recorded as discovered work, not scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Loss bound (AC1).** A page reload/crash mid-run, followed by the run's
   final upload, loses no more than the records not yet confirmed by the dev
   server — the in-flight batch (≤64 records / ~1.3 s at defaults) plus the ring
   buffer's unflushed tail (<64 records); everything confirmed is recoverable
   from the dev server. The bound holds while the dev server is reachable; during
   an outage the un-uploaded tail remains in memory and is retried at run end.
2. **Exactly once + one evaluation (AC2).** A run's stored session file contains
   each record exactly once across any mix of partial and final uploads (no
   duplication, no gaps from lost/retried 2xx responses) and the automatic
   evaluation runs exactly once per completed run.
3. **CLI tooling unchanged (AC3).** `npm run record`, `npm run capture` and
   `npm run verify-dev-telemetry` behave unchanged — the page buffer is never
   cleared mid-run and `window.__aiHellTelemetry.read()` returns the full run
   after run end; `verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` passes unchanged (one
   `session-*.jsonl` per run, one evaluation artifact set, all dev uploads 200,
   zero uploads/recordings when the share setting is off). `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs`
   behaviour is unchanged.
4. **Testing/validation.** New hermetic tests cover: the streamer sends one part
   per flush in order; a lost 2xx is retried from the last confirmed offset and
   the server deduplicates (no duplication, no gaps); an unreachable server
   leaves the watermark unadvanced and the buffer intact; run end finalises once
   and triggers one evaluation; the sink buffer is never cleared mid-run; and
   `startRun` starts a fresh run key (no cross-run mixing). Server-side tests
   cover part staging, gap rejection, finalise/rename and single-evaluation.
5. **Docs.** `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` and
   `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` describe the streaming part protocol, the
   loss bound, the offline/retry behaviour and the crashed-run partial
   location/semantics. All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
   entries.
6. **Dev-only containment.** Streaming is behind the existing dev gate and is
   absent from a production bundle (bundle-hygiene markers updated for any new
   protocol strings); the opt-out setting produces zero part uploads.
7. **Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (via
   the test-skill runner; enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- **Dev-only.** Reuse `isDevTelemetryUploadEnabled` / `loadDevTelemetryUploader`;
  no production bundle may contain the part protocol or the streamer.
- **Preserve the page buffer.** Never clear the in-memory sink mid-run — the CLI
  tooling and `verify-dev-telemetry`'s non-empty-buffer assertion depend on it;
  only the upload watermark moves.
- **Same endpoint path** (`/api/telemetry/upload`) plus an explicit part marker,
  so `verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` observes the parts and the existing
  bundle-hygiene marker remains valid. Keep the whole-file (no-marker) contract
  byte-compatible.
- **Bounded bodies.** Each part is ≤1 batch (tens of KB). The run-end tail after
  an offline stretch still respects the 8 MiB CDP-message cap (client) and the
  16 MiB server body bound; over-cap behaviour keeps today's actionable skip.
- **Ordered, exactly-once parts.** Serialise part POSTs; dedupe by a
  server-authoritative cumulative offset; reject gaps.
- **No cross-run mixing.** A new `runKey` and a buffer reset at `startRun`; a
  crashed run's partial is never merged into another run.
- **No new runtime dependency.** Node built-ins and already-imported modules
  only; tests write only into `mkdtempSync` temp dirs (suite-write guard).
- **Repository boundaries.** Do not edit `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/` or other
  agent infrastructure.
- **Coordination.** Do not implement concurrently in the same worktree as the
  in-memory-sink item (already shipped) or the CLI-local salvage item
  (`AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/telemetry/sinks.ts` — add the optional post-flush observer seam on the
  dev JSONL sink (delta NDJSON per batch); keep the buffer/`reset()` semantics.
- `src/telemetry/devStream.ts` *(new)* — dev-only streaming uploader: serialised
  part POSTs, watermark/offset tracking, bounded retry/backoff, final part.
- `src/telemetry/devUpload.ts` — evolve the run-end uploader into the final-part
  sender (or add a `final` mode), keeping the 8 MiB cap and fire-and-forget
  contract.
- `src/telemetry/devMode.ts` — dev-gated loader for the streamer (static
  elimination in production, mirroring `loadDevTelemetryUploader`).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/core/runTelemetry.ts` — wire the
  streamer to the sink observer and the run-end final part; keep
  `window.__aiHellTelemetry` returning the full buffer.
- `src/telemetry/recorder.ts` — expose a flush/batch observer only if the sink
  seam alone is insufficient.
- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` — part protocol: run-keyed staging,
  offset dedupe, finalise/rename, single evaluation; whole-file path unchanged.
- Tests — `src/telemetry/devStream.test.ts` *(new)*, `sinks.test.ts`,
  `devUpload.test.ts`, `recorder.test.ts`, `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlaySceneTelemetry.test.ts`; `scripts/verify-dev-telemetry.mjs`
  stays green unchanged.
- `scripts/check-bundle-hygiene.mjs` — add/confirm forbidden markers for any new
  dev protocol string.
- Docs — `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`,
  `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`.

## Related work

- **Control scheme reverts to Asteroids after re-opening Settings** (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3, completed) — the in-memory, per-run dev sink this item extends; it explicitly deferred incremental upload here.
- **Recorder silently loses a session when the browser is closed instead of Ctrl+C** (AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ, plan_complete) — **partial overlap, different scope**: CLI-local checkpoint/salvage of a mid-run close. Its decision D1 records that if page streaming ships first, its checkpoint becomes redundant and its salvage message should point at the server-side partial. This item changes what the **server** has; that item changes what the **CLI** does when the page dies. Its AC requires `record-session` behaviour unchanged, which this item preserves.
- **Game-side uploader fired at run end** (AH-0MVBMRK6X0069QDI, completed) — the `uploadDevTelemetry` flow being extended; its 8 MiB CDP cap still applies.
- **Dev-only telemetry gate helper + enforcement scan** (AH-0MVBMR0BG0005BBI, completed) and **Dev collection-on-by-default in stock dev mode** (AH-0MVBMRIB800201KK, completed) — the gate the streamer must reuse and the opt-out path it must honour.
- **Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling** (AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ, completed) — the CLI tools whose buffer-read contract AC3 preserves.
- **Capture crashes on long full-run clips: Playwright CDP pipe overflows** (AH-0MVN06MS9007LRKE, completed) and **Cap the dev upload message size** (AH-0MVNVGP55002G0KH, completed) — why every upload stays bounded.
- **Production telemetry: opt-in consent, privacy, remote sink** (AH-0MUY08Y9P005ER7A, completed) — `HttpTelemetryTransport` already streams batches with retry/backoff; the dev path should mirror its semantics.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — harness coupling.** Any part stored under the `session-*.jsonl` glob
  mid-run breaks `verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` (it takes the newest match as the
  finished recording). Mitigation: stage under `recordings/parts/` and rename on
  finalise.
- **Risk — exactly-once subtlety.** A lost 2xx means the client cannot know
  whether the part landed. Mitigation: server-authoritative cumulative offset,
  client advances only on confirmation, re-send from the confirmed offset,
  server truncates the already-appended prefix and rejects gaps.
- **Risk — ordering.** Concurrent parts could interleave records. Mitigation:
  serialise the part chain (as the recorder already serialises sink writes).
- **Risk — offline backlog.** A long outage grows the run-end tail until it hits
  the 8 MiB CDP cap and is skipped (today's behaviour). Accepted for dev
  telemetry; documented.
- **Risk — bundle hygiene.** A new protocol string could leak into `dist/`.
  Mitigation: extend `scripts/check-bundle-hygiene.mjs` forbidden markers and
  keep the streamer behind the statically-eliminated dev loader.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Partial janitors, a server-side recovery UI, IndexedDB,
  alerting, or changing flush cadence are out of scope — record them as
  `discovered-from:AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD` items instead.
- **Assumption A1.** Defaults: full sampling, ~50.8 ticks/s, 64-record batches →
  ~1.26 s/batch. The loss bound scales with `VITE_TELEMETRY_SAMPLE_RATE` and
  `VITE_TELEMETRY_BATCH_SIZE`.
- **Assumption A2.** A run key of `<startedAt>-<runSeed>` (or a random id) is
  unique in practice; `startRun` already knows both values.
- **Assumption A3.** "Exactly once" is scoped per run; a crashed run's partial is
  never merged into another run.
- **Assumption A4.** Losing the current ring-buffer tail (<1 batch) in addition
  to the in-flight batch is acceptable; a strict one-batch bound would need a
  shorter flush cadence or `bufferCapacity == batchSize`, which can be tuned at
  implementation time if the producer prefers.
- **Priority rationale:** kept `low` — dev-only telemetry that is conveniently
  re-recordable, not product data loss, and not blocking other work. The
  in-memory-sink work already removed the user-facing regression (settings
  becoming unsaveable); this item bounds the residual loss for interrupted dev
  runs.

- **Q — Which proposed design should be adopted: per-batch part protocol, or a
  heartbeat/checkpoint?** — Answer (agent, repo evidence + item text):
  **part protocol on the existing endpoint** (option 1). It streams every flushed
  batch, so the ≤1-batch bound holds without a separate recovery-on-demand path;
  a heartbeat still needs a reload recovery mechanism and cannot beat the bound
  unless it also fires per batch. Evidence: `src/telemetry/sinks.ts`
  (per-run buffer), `src/telemetry/devUpload.ts` (run-end POST),

  full run through `window.__aiHellTelemetry` **after** the run ends, and
  `verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` asserts the buffer is non-empty
  (`happySinkChars > 0`). The design therefore streams deltas via a watermark and
  never clears the sink mid-run. Evidence: `scripts/verify-dev-telemetry.mjs`
  L~147, `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_initTelemetry`/`flushAndUploadDevTelemetry`.

  `telemetry upload crash resilience batch`, `incremental batch upload dev

  mid-run-close UX; AH-0MVN06MS9007LRKE / AH-0MVNVGP55002G0KH are the bounded-

  buffer's unflushed tail (<64 records), worst case ≈127 records / ~2.5 s,

# Implement the Music System defined by the Audio Design Chapter

## Goal

Build the runtime background-music system for AI Hell against the fixed design contract captured in
`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (produced by **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)**).

User story: *As a player, I want a dynamic, retro-arcade soundtrack that responds to combat intensity, so
that runs feel like the relentless survival experience the game is aiming for; and as a developer I want the
music engine driven by a documented parameter/state contract, so behaviour is testable and reproducible.*

> **Scope stance:** this is **future scope, out of MVP** (GDD §8). The MVP ships baked ToneForge SFX only
> (GDD §7.3), and §7.3 remains authoritative for SFX. This item must **not** be started until the design
> chapter exists and has been reviewed, and it must **not** promote music into the MVP without an explicit
> producer decision.

## Background

- AI Hell currently has **no background music** by design: GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope, and the
  player-fire grid is deliberately quantised to a **silent internal 80 BPM beat** (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- SFX are build-time baked WAV assets rendered deterministically by ToneForge and played through Phaser's
  shared `AudioContext` (`src/audio/effects.ts`); the authoritative cue catalogue is
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.
- The Audio Design Chapter specifies the musical identity (Phrygian Dominant combat scale, Lydian ambient
  scale, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), instrumentation palette, dynamic-mixing rules, state-driven
  transitions, parameter mapping, audio budget and accessibility requirements.

## Expected behaviour and outcomes

- A music system that plays layered/stemmed music driven by an explicit game-state parameter, with
  bar-boundary transitions, stingers, and ducking, as specified by the chapter.
- Music state follows gameplay (e.g. menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-health tension, run end) with the
  transition rules and timings given in the chapter, and never disrupts the beat grid or the SFX mix.
- Reproducible, deterministic behaviour suitable for automated tests; no audio regressions to the shipped SFX
  pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Contract traceable to the chapter:** every implemented music state, transition, stinger and mixing parameter traces to a named section of `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`, recorded in a mapping table in the implementation docs.
- [ ] **AC2 — Musical content matches the documented identity:** the delivered cues/stems use the chapter's scales, motifs and progressions (Phrygian Dominant combat, Lydian ambient, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), verified by an explicit audit table (motif → scale degrees → usage state).
- [ ] **AC3 — State machine implemented and tested:** transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified), with unit tests covering each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid/reset paths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Dynamic mixing implemented:** ducking, per-layer volume targets and the priority tiers behave as specified; SFX intelligibility is preserved (music ducks under key SFX cues) and is covered by tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.
- [ ] **AC6 — Budget met:** the shipped music respects the chapter's audio budget (memory, streaming, polyphony, layer count) on the supported targets, measured and recorded.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs updated:** GDD §7.3 and §8 are updated to reflect the shipped music system, and `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` is marked as implemented for the sections that ship.
- [ ] **AC8 — No SFX regression:** the existing ToneForge baked-SFX pipeline and cue catalogue remain unchanged and their tests pass; any chapter §6.4 procedural SFX recipes are explicitly **not** adopted unless decisioned separately.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project build and test suite pass.**

## Constraints

- **Blocked by** the docs item **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item
  must not begin before `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists.
- Music stays **out of MVP scope** until a producer decision promotes it (GDD §7.3, §8).
- Keep the gameplay SVG/vector aesthetic and retro-arcade palette of the chapter; UK English in all docs.
- §7.3 (baked ToneForge SFX) remains authoritative for SFX; the chapter is an addendum whose §6.4 procedural
  SFX recipes are design reference only.
- Prefer reusing the existing audio plumbing (`src/audio/effects.ts`, shared `AudioContext`, manifest-driven
  playback) over introducing new runtime dependencies; any middleware adoption (the chapter's FMOD/Wwise
  guidance) is a separate decision — the web build currently has no middleware.

## Approach (indicative)

1. Confirm scope with the producer (MVP vs post-MVP) and record the decision on this item.
2. Ingest the chapter into an implementation mapping table (state → parameter → cue/stem set → transition).
3. Decide the delivery mechanism (baked stems via ToneForge + `AudioContext` playback, per the existing
   pipeline) versus a runtime synthesiser; record the trade-off before coding.
4. Implement the music state machine and mixing layer behind a single facade, mirroring the existing SFX
   façade style; add unit tests per transition and per mixing rule.
5. Add accessibility controls and the autoplay guard; verify budget and measure on target hardware.
6. Update GDD §7.3/§8 and the chapter's implemented-sections marker.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` — the design contract (prerequisite)
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — existing SFX façade / shared `AudioContext` plumbing to reuse
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — where combat-state music parameters would be driven from
- `src/core/rules.ts` — game-rules config (including `beatBpm`) that music tempo must stay coherent with
- `src/audio/` — new music module + tests
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 and §8 updates

## Risks & assumptions

- **Overlap with the shipped silent beat grid (medium):** player fire is quantised to an internal 80 BPM beat.
  Music must be tempo-coherent with that grid or the two will fight; assume music tempo is either locked to
  `beatBpm` or documented as intentionally independent.
- **Chapter/SFX divergence (medium):** the chapter's §6.4 procedural SFX recipes differ from the shipped baked
  catalogue; §7.3 stays authoritative (AC8).
- **Middleware assumption (low):** the chapter's FMOD/Wwise guidance is forward-looking; no middleware exists in
  the web build, so it is design intent only.
- **Scope creep into MVP (medium):** music is out of MVP; promotion needs an explicit producer decision.

## Related work

- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — prerequisite; produces the design contract.
- discovered-from:AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W
- GDD §7.3 (SFX, authoritative for MVP), GDD §8 (Future Scope — "Background music"), and
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (SFX cue catalogue).
- Beat grid / timing context: AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B (beat-aligned fire grid), AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3 (beat-timed
  explosion accents).

# Recorder silently loses a session when the browser is closed instead of Ctrl+C

**Issue type:** bug · **Priority:** medium · **Reported:** 2026-10-30 (operator, dev tooling) · **Discovered-from:** AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX

**Headline:** `npm run record` keeps the whole run's telemetry in the page's in-memory buffer and only writes it after the wait loop exits cleanly, so closing the browser window instead of pressing Ctrl+C throws `Target page, context or browser has been closed` from `page.waitForTimeout`, exits non-zero with a raw Playwright error, and writes **nothing** — a long human session is unrecoverable. Make an interrupted recording recoverable (a crash-safe partial capture) or at minimum fail with one actionable line naming the file that was not written and the correct stop procedure, and state the stop requirement (and the `npm run record -- --auto` separator form) in the tool's usage text and docs.

## Problem statement

`scripts/record-session.mjs` starts Vite with `VITE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true VITE_TELEMETRY_SINK=jsonl`, launches Chromium, and polls `readRunEndedSignal` in a `while (!stop.requested)` loop with `page.waitForTimeout(options.pollMs)`. The run's telemetry lives **only** in the page's in-memory buffer, exposed through the dev-gated `window.__aiHellTelemetry` accessor (telemetry never uses `localStorage`, AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3). The buffer is drained to disk — `resolveRecordingOutputPath` → `writeFileSync` — **after** the loop. Two consequences:

- **Browser close or page crash mid-recording loses everything.** The `waitForTimeout` (or the next `page.evaluate`) throws a target-closed Playwright error; `main()`'s rejection handler prints the raw message (`page.waitForTimeout: Target page, context or browser has been closed`) and exits 1. No recording is written, no path is named, and nothing tells the operator that the session is gone or how to avoid it next time.
- **The stop procedure is unstated where it is needed.** `--help` lists `[--auto]` and the docs mention Ctrl+C, but neither the usage text nor the failure path says "closing the browser loses the session; press Ctrl+C in the terminal to save". Related: `npm run record --auto` does not reach the script as a flag (npm consumes it) — the working form is `npm run record -- --auto` — and nothing in the tool's own output says so.

This item is the dev-tooling behaviour on a **local** recording. Page-side streaming of telemetry to the dev server (which would bound the loss at one batch by uploading during the run) is a separate, parked item — see the boundary in *Related work*.

## Users

- **Developer / operator running a human session** — "As a developer, when I record a long human session and I close the browser window (or the page crashes) instead of pressing Ctrl+C, I want whatever was captured to be saved, or at least to be told in one line which file was not written and how to record properly next time — I do not want to discover after an hour of play that the recording is gone."
- **Developer reading the tooling** — "As a developer, I want `npm run record --help` and the recording docs to state the stop procedure (Ctrl+C saves; closing the window does not) and the correct `--auto` invocation, so the mistake is avoidable in the first place."
- **Maintainer of the recording tooling** — "As a maintainer, I want the interruption path to be a testable seam (injected page/fs), so the crash path cannot regress into a raw Playwright stack again."

## Existing state (verified in code, `dev` @ 59d40269a)

- `scripts/record-session.mjs`
  - `main()` builds the output path **after** the loop (`resolveRecordingOutputPath(options.output, options)`) — so even the would-be filename does not exist at crash time; the default name is stamped at write time, not at start time.
  - Poll loop: `while (!stop.requested) { decoded = decodeRunEndedDetail(await page.evaluate(readRunEndedSignal)); if (decoded !== null && options.auto) break; if (Date.now() - startedAt >= options.maxDurationMs) break; await page.waitForTimeout(options.pollMs); }`.
  - `createStopController()` handles SIGINT/SIGTERM only — there is no `page.on('close')`, `page.on('crash')` or `browser.on('disconnected')` listener, and no distinction between stop reasons.
  - The buffer is read once, after the loop, through `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks` (bounded CDP messages).
  - `finally` closes the browser/server; the loop's target-closed error escapes to the top-level handler, which prints `error.message` and `process.exit(1)`.
  - Usage text (`--help`) mentions `[--auto]` but not the Ctrl+C-to-save requirement nor the `npm run record -- --auto` separator form.
- Reusable seams already in `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`: `readDevTelemetryChunk({ offset, chunkChars })` returns `{ total, chunk }` — a bounded, incremental slice reader with buffer-reset detection — and `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks` shows the "total changed ⇒ discard the partial read" rule. Both are plain exported functions, so an incremental checkpoint can reuse them without new page-side code.
- Precedent for the failure UX: `scripts/capture-salvage.mjs` (`salvageFailedCapture`, `formatSalvageMessage`) prints **one** actionable line first (what failed, bytes salvaged, the `.partial.webm` path, next action) and exits non-zero; `scripts/capture-chunk-sink.mjs` writes to `<stem>.partial.webm` and renames into place only on success. The recording tool has no equivalent.
- Docs to keep true: `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` §1 (flag table; "On Ctrl+C the tool still exports whatever the sink has already flushed … so an interrupted run yields a partial but valid recording" — true only for Ctrl+C, not for a browser close), and `docs/TELEMETRY.md` L117–122 / L566–574 (the recorder reads the buffer through `window.__aiHellTelemetry`).
- Test coverage today: `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` covers argument parsing, path resolution, the balance artifact and the `--help`/argv entry guard; `scripts/recording.test.ts` covers the pure recording library. **Nothing** exercises `main()`'s wait loop, the stop reasons, or the browser-close path — `main()` is not reachable without a real browser, which is why the crash path is untested.
- Not covered by this item: the page already POSTs the run to `POST /api/telemetry/upload` at run end (`PlayScene._finishRun()`), so a run that **ended** before the window was closed is already stored server-side; the loss is confined to a run closed mid-run.

## Desired change

1. **Crash-safe partial capture (recommended).** Resolve the output path **before** the browser launches. While recording, checkpoint the page buffer to a documented partial file next to it (`<output>.partial.jsonl`) on an interval (`--checkpoint-ms`, default 15 000 ms, `0` disables), appending **only new bytes** through the incremental `readDevTelemetryChunk` offset loop, and restarting from offset 0 when the reported `total` shrinks (the game started a new run — never mix two runs in one file, mirroring `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks`). On a clean stop (Ctrl+C, run end, `--max-duration`) write the final file exactly as today and remove the partial. On a browser close / page crash, finalise the partial as the salvaged session and print one actionable line naming it.
2. **Actionable failure when nothing was captured.** If no bytes were captured (or the buffer is unreachable), print exactly one actionable first line — `Recording lost: the browser was closed before Ctrl+C — run npm run record and press Ctrl+C to save` — naming the resolved output path that was **not** written and the correct stop procedure, and exit non-zero. A raw Playwright target-closed message must never be the only diagnostic.
3. **Usage and docs.** `--help` and the docs state: press Ctrl+C in the terminal to finish and save; closing the browser window ends the recording and (at best) salvages a partial file; `--auto` must be passed after `--` (`npm run record -- --auto`).
4. **A testable seam.** Extract the wait/finalise logic into exported, injectable functions (page `evaluate`, fs writes, clock) so the crash, salvage and clean-stop paths are covered hermetically in `scripts/record-session.test.ts` — no real browser in the suite.

**Recorded design decisions (settle at review if the producer prefers otherwise; none blocks intake):**

- **D1 — Local checkpoint, not page streaming.** The fix stays inside `scripts/` (CLI-side). Streaming telemetry to the dev server mid-run is AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD and is out of scope; if that lands first, this item's checkpoint becomes redundant and the salvage message can point at the server-side partial (a follow-up, not part of this work).
- **D2 — Salvage-then-message, not message-only.** The item's own AC1 allows either branch; the recommendation is to implement both, so a long session is actually recoverable and the message path still covers "nothing captured".
- **D3 — Partial path.** `<resolved output>.partial.jsonl` (e.g. `recordings/session-2026-10-30T21-18-30-585Z.jsonl.partial.jsonl`), inside the already-gitignored `recordings/`. A salvage must never overwrite an existing final recording — use a collision-safe name (numeric suffix) if the target exists, mirroring the dev-upload plugin's collision-safe storage.
- **D4 — No balance artifact for a salvaged partial.** `balance-stats.json` is written only for a clean stop; a salvaged partial is an interrupted run, not a completed one, and the message says so.
- **D5 — Exit codes.** `0` on a clean stop; `1` (non-zero) on an interrupted/crashed recording, whether salvaged or lost — parity with `capture-salvage`.
- **D6 — Default filename stamp becomes the start time.** Resolving the path up front is required for the partial path; the only visible effect is that the default `session-<timestamp>.jsonl` stamp names when recording started.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Browser close mid-recording never silently discards the session.** When the page/browser closes (or crashes) during the wait loop, the recorder writes whatever telemetry had been captured — at least the last checkpointed records, each a complete newline-terminated record that parses through the existing recording reader (`parseTelemetryJsonl` / `parseRecording`), never a half-written line — to the documented partial path (`<output>.partial.jsonl`, collision-safe) and prints **one** actionable line naming that path and the Ctrl+C stop procedure; when nothing was captured it prints exactly one actionable line — `Recording lost: the browser was closed before Ctrl+C — run npm run record and press Ctrl+C to save` — naming the resolved output path that was not written. No Playwright target-closed message is the only diagnostic, and the process exits non-zero. On a clean stop (Ctrl+C / run end / `--max-duration`) the final recording is byte-identical to today's output, no partial file remains, and the exit code is unchanged.
2. **The interruption path is covered by hermetic tests.** New tests (`scripts/record-session.test.ts`, node environment, no real browser — page/fs/clock injected) prove: (a) a target-closed error thrown from the poll loop routes to the salvage path and not to a raw error exit; (b) with zero captured bytes the lost message names the output path and the Ctrl+C procedure; (c) a clean stop writes the final file and removes the partial; (d) the checkpoint appends only new bytes and restarts at offset 0 when the reported buffer `total` shrinks (no two-run mixing); (e) a salvage never overwrites an existing final recording. `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` keeps passing, extended where it asserts the usage text.
3. **Usage text and docs state the stop requirement.** `npm run record --help` (and `node scripts/record-session.mjs --help`) states the Ctrl+C-to-save requirement, that closing the browser window does not save a completed recording (at best a partial), and the `npm run record -- --auto` separator form; asserted by a test on the help output.
4. **Documentation.** `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` §1 (flag table + the Ctrl+C paragraph) and the recorder paragraphs in `docs/TELEMETRY.md` document the partial path, partial-vs-final semantics, the salvage/lost behaviour, the checkpoint flag and the stop procedure. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Scope ladder.** Only `scripts/record-session.mjs`, a new `scripts/record-session.test.ts`, small additions to `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` and the two docs above (+ a `.d.mts` update if a new export needs it). **No** changes under `src/`, no new page-side API, no dev-server/upload-protocol change (AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD), no change to the telemetry schema.
- **Reuse the bounded read seams.** Checkpoint and final reads go through `readDevTelemetryChunk` / `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks` — never a whole-buffer single CDP message (the string-size overflow class is AH-0MVNVGP55002G0KH).
- **Preserve the clean path.** Ctrl+C, `--auto`, `--max-duration`, `--poll`, `--seed`, `--bot`, `--bot-config`, `--json` and the `balance-stats.json` artifact behave exactly as today; the printed success output keeps its current lines (a salvaged/lost line is additive).
- **Bounded I/O on long runs.** The checkpoint must be append-only and incremental: no per-tick full re-read of the buffer, and no unbounded in-process buffering of the recording. Append only up to the last newline in each chunk (never a partial record), carrying the remainder into the next read.
- **No tracked data writes.** Recordings and partials stay under `recordings/` (gitignored); tests write only into `mkdtempSync` temp dirs, so the suite never dirties the checkout (suite-write guard, AH-0MVS9TY0N0034LZT).
- **Repository boundaries.** Do not edit `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/` or other agent infrastructure.
- **No new runtime dependency.** Node built-ins plus the already-imported Playwright/Vite modules only.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/record-session.mjs` — `main()`, `createStopController()`, `resolveRecordingOutputPath()`, `resolveBalanceStatsOutputPath()`, the `--help` block; resolve the output up front, add stop reasons, the checkpoint writer, the salvage/lost finaliser and the `--checkpoint-ms` flag.

# Checkpointed crash-safe partial capture and salvage

**Parent:** AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ — Recorder silently loses a session when the browser is closed instead of Ctrl+C.
**Depends on:** child 1 (interruption seam and hermetic crash-path tests).

## Goal

As a **developer recording a long human session**, when I close the browser window (or the page crashes) instead of pressing Ctrl+C, I want whatever was captured saved to a documented partial file, so an hour of play is not lost outright.

The run lives only in the page's in-memory buffer (`window.__aiHellTelemetry`); today `main()` drains it to disk once, after the wait loop, so a closed page has nothing to read. Checkpoint the buffer incrementally to `<output>.partial.jsonl` while recording and finalise that partial as the salvaged session when the page dies.

## Scope

- Resolve the recording output path (`resolveRecordingOutputPath`) **before** the browser launches, so the partial path exists at crash time; the default `session-<timestamp>.jsonl` stamp becomes the **start** time.
- Add `--checkpoint-ms MS` (default `15000`, `0` disables) to `parseRecordArgs`, the flag table and the `--help` block.
- Checkpoint writer: on each interval, read **only new bytes** via the incremental `readDevTelemetryChunk` offset loop (reuse the seam; never a whole-buffer single CDP message — AH-0MVNVGP55002G0KH), append only up to the last newline (never a half-written record; carry the remainder into the next read), and restart from offset 0 when the reported `total` shrinks (the game started a new run — never mix two runs in one file, mirroring `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks`).
- On a `target_closed` stop, finalise the partial as the salvaged session: collision-safe name (numeric suffix) so a salvage never overwrites an existing final recording (mirror the dev-upload plugin's collision-safe storage), print **one** actionable line naming the partial path and the Ctrl+C stop procedure, exit 1. Do **not** write `balance-stats.json` for a salvaged partial.
- On a clean stop (Ctrl+C / run end / `--max-duration`): write the final file exactly as today, remove the partial, write `balance-stats.json` as today, exit 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Browser close mid-recording never silently discards the session.** When the page/browser closes (or crashes) during the wait loop, the recorder writes whatever telemetry had been captured — at least the last checkpointed records, each a complete newline-terminated record that parses through the existing recording reader (`parseTelemetryJsonl` / `parseRecording`), never a half-written line — to the documented partial path (`<output>.partial.jsonl`, collision-safe) and prints **one** actionable line naming that path and the Ctrl+C stop procedure; the process exits non-zero. The checkpoint appends only new bytes and restarts at offset 0 when the reported buffer `total` shrinks (no two-run mixing), and a salvage never overwrites an existing final recording — both proven in `scripts/record-session.test.ts`. On a clean stop (Ctrl+C / run end / `--max-duration`) the final recording is byte-identical to today's output, no partial file remains, the exit code is unchanged, and no `balance-stats.json` is written for a salvaged partial.
2. `scripts/record-session.test.ts` proves the checkpoint appends only new bytes and restarts at offset 0 when the reported buffer `total` shrinks (no two-run mixing).
3. `scripts/record-session.test.ts` proves a salvage never overwrites an existing final recording (collision-safe numeric suffix).
4. `--checkpoint-ms` (default 15000, `0` disables) is parsed, covered by `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts` argument-parsing assertions, and passed through to the checkpoint writer.
5. The checkpoint appends only new bytes through the incremental `readDevTelemetryChunk` offset loop — no per-tick full re-read of the buffer, no unbounded in-process buffering — and every written line parses through `parseTelemetryJsonl`.
6. A salvaged partial and its message are additive: the clean-path success output, `balance-stats.json` and exit code are exactly as today.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/record-session.mjs` — output path resolved up front, `--checkpoint-ms`, checkpoint writer, salvage finaliser, stop-reason handling.
- `scripts/record-session.test.ts` — checkpoint append/reset and no-overwrite tests.
- `scripts/record-session.d.mts` — declarations for new exports and the `checkpointMs` option.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — `readDevTelemetryChunk` / `readDevTelemetryBufferInChunks` (reused, not modified).
- `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` — flag row added to the table (prose/behaviour documented in child 3).

## Notes

- Recordings and partials stay under the gitignored `recordings/`; tests write only into `mkdtempSync` temp dirs.
- Long-run cost risk: one CDP round-trip plus a small append per interval; the final read still uses the existing whole-buffer chunked reader. Measurement is child 4.
- This child extends child 1's single rescue seam with the partial-writing branch; it does not add a second failure path.
- If AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD (page → dev-server streaming) ships first, this local checkpoint becomes redundant and the salvage message should point at the server-side partial — a follow-up, not part of this child.

# Context

The ring-timing harness (AH-0MVUXCBQY001ESWT) measured both Hangar War ring
budgets with the headless arena. Both land inside the design windows (ring 1:
**43.7 min** in 40–60; ring 2: **91.6 min** in 70–100), but ring 2's
composition is lopsided.

- Ring 2's authored aggression floor is **3** (`src/data/hex-ring-2.csv`), which
  the shipped `hexAggressionLevel` mapping resolves to campaign level 4 — the
  first level where enemies fire. The competent bot survives the full
  ≈5-minute deployment window at levels 1–3 and loses every run at level 4+, so
  **all 12 ring-2 deployments are first-attempt losses**.
- The ring-2 total is therefore dominated by the modelled retry allowance
  (**60 of 91.6 min**), not by measured deployment time (7.6 min). The design's
  estimate of "≈60 minutes of deployments plus 10–40 minutes of builds and
  losses" does not hold at ring 2's authored aggressions.

Evidence: `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` (seeds 1–3, competent bot) and
`docs/EVALUATION.md` § Ring timing harness.

# Goal

As a maintainer, I want ring 2's aggression floor reviewed against the design's

`src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts` » `records the measured ring timings and their tolerance` pins the four measured ring-timing means as literals:

expect(spec).toMatch(/49\.2/);
expect(spec).toMatch(/109\.0/);

The GDD §8.2 table those assertions guard is a *transcription* of `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` (the artifact the same test already asserts is cited). - AH-0MVXSHAS100010S0 (ring-2 budget/measurements) — no, stale only after the wrap-aware bot landed;
- AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG (wrap-aware bot) raised the measured grind 91.6 → 109.0 min;

## Problem

`scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune` edits a tracked balance CSV in place and journals the pre-edit bytes beside it (`src/data/<file>.tune-journal`). Both paths are process-global, not per-run:

1. **Startup reconcile steals a live journal.** `main()` reconciles `<csv>.tune-journal` before anything else (crash recovery). A journal is written before the edit and removed after the restore, so it exists for the whole candidate sweep of a *running* process — a second `--tune` run on the same CSV reconciles it, restoring the CSV underneath run 1.
2. **Two runs interleave edits.** Run 2 writes its own journal over run 1's, then restores from run 2's bytes while run 1 continues its candidate sweep against a file run 2 may have rewritten.

Discovered while fixing AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS: the `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` watchdog case asserted "no `*.tune-journal` anywhere in `src/data`", which failed when a sibling suite in the same parallel Vitest run held a journal at the same shared path. The suite was fixed for the shared path (the assertion is now scoped to the run's own pid), but the product-level hazard remains for real concurrent CLI invocations.

## Impact

Two designers (or a designer plus a scripted tuning sweep) tuning the same balance CSV at once can silently produce a comparison against the wrong CSV bytes, and the crash-recovery journal can be consumed by the wrong run. Single-run usage is unaffected.

## Suggested approach

Pick one, cheapest first:

- **Lock file**: an exclusive `<csv>.tune-lock` (O\_EXCL) held for the whole run, with a bounded wait and a clear exit-2 diagnostic naming the holder pid. The journal's pid is already recorded, so the holder is identifiable.
- **Refuse concurrent runs**: on `writeJournal`, if a journal exists whose pid is alive (`kill(pid, 0)`), abort with exit 2 naming that pid instead of overwriting it.
- **Per-run temp CSVs**: out of scope — `--tune` deliberately edits the tracked file so the candidate sweep reads it through the shared config store.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Two concurrent `--tune` runs on the same CSV cannot interleave: the second either waits (bounded) or exits non-zero with a diagnostic naming the holding pid.
2. A live journal is never reconciled by another process: crash recovery only consumes a journal whose pid is dead.
3. `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` and `scripts/csvEditJournal.test.ts` still pass, including the pid-scoped journal assertions added by AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS.
4. `docs/BALANCING.md` documents the concurrency rule alongside the crash-safe journal section.
5. Full suite passes (`/skill:test`).

## Related work

- discovered-from:AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS (the test-failure item that surfaced the shared-path race).

## Goal / user story

As a player in a late-game wave, I want hundreds of asteroids on screen at once
without the game dropping frames, so that the asteroid hazard stays fun rather
than turning into a stutter-fest.

The operator asked whether asteroids can be "managed on the GPU" to improve
performance when hundreds are on screen, on the assumption that they are all
essentially the same.

## What the code does today (investigated before filing)

The premise "they are all essentially the same" is **not** true of the current
implementation — and that is the root of the cost:

- Every asteroid draws a **unique** seeded jagged polygon in
  `Asteroid._drawBody()` (7–9 jittered vertices per rock). So each rock is its
  own silhouette, not a shared one.
- `BaseEnemy._addStaticBodyLayer()` bakes each silhouette into a canvas texture
  via `bakeEnemyBodyTexture()` (`src/utils/enemyBodyTextures.ts`), but:
  - the cache is keyed by a hash of the drawn commands, so **unique asteroid
    shapes never share a texture** — every asteroid is a distinct texture and
    therefore a distinct draw call (no batching);
  - the cache is capped at `MAX_BAKED_ENEMY_BODY_TEXTURES = 64` **per game**,
    shared with every enemy type. Once the cap is hit, new silhouettes keep
    their `Phaser.GameObjects.Graphics` body, which is re-tessellated and
    re-submitted **every frame** — precisely the hotspot the baked-texture work
    removed for other enemies (`docs/PERFORMANCE.md`).
- Each asteroid is also a `Phaser.GameObjects.Container`
  (`ContainerWebGLRenderer` is a measured hotspot), with its own per-frame
  position/rotation update.

Asteroid volume can genuinely reach the hundreds: `computeSpawns()` in
`src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` doubles the per-wave count every 8 waves
(`2 * 2^floor((wave+1)/8)`) and is unbounded, and every large/medium rock
splits into two children (1 large -> 7 destroyed enemies per chain).

## Options considered

### Option A — shared cosmetic shape pool + single texture atlas (recommended)

Pre-generate a small fixed set of asteroid silhouettes per size tier (e.g. 8–12
shapes) once, into **one texture atlas**; assign each asteroid a variant
deterministically from its seed. Asteroids then render as plain `Image` sprites
sharing one texture, so Phaser batches all of them into a single draw call, and
rotation/scale/position are free per-sprite GPU transforms.

- Reuses the existing baked-texture architecture and the `BaseEnemy` seam.
- Keeps the jagged-rock look; a handful of distinct looks is indistinguishable
  at asteroid size.
- Bounded texture usage (no more exhausting the 64-texture budget, no
  `Graphics` per-frame fallback).
- Low risk, preserves gym↔game parity (shared code in `BaseEnemy`/`Asteroid`).

### Option B — true GPU instancing (custom render node / shader mesh)

One asteroid geometry + a per-instance transform buffer updated each frame; a
vertex shader applies position/rotation/scale. Maximum throughput (one draw call
for *all* asteroids), but Phaser 4 has no built-in instancing API, it bypasses
the entity/`Container` render path, and it risks diverging from the shared
gym↔game core. Higher effort and risk; worth it only if Option A is not enough.

### Option C — render all asteroids into one RenderTexture per frame

Still CPU draw submission each frame; does not remove the cost. Not recommended.

## Recommendation

Do **Option A** first: it captures most of the batching win within the current
architecture and fixes the texture-cache exhaustion and per-frame `Graphics`
fallback. Measure it against a reproducible asteroid stress scenario; only
escalate to Option B if the GPU-batched sprite path still misses the budget.

## Measurement prerequisite

No reproducible "hundreds of asteroids" stress scenario exists today — the
shared `GymPerformance` stress gym is 100 firing *ships*, not asteroids. Before
claiming any improvement we need one (a new asteroid stress gym, or a
variant/launch setup of `GymPerformance`) and a before/after
`npm run perf:measure` pair on the same host, per `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` rules.

## Operator decisions (2026-11-06)

The operator answered the open questions; the work proceeds on these decisions:

1. **Shared palette is acceptable.** A small fixed palette of shared asteroid
   silhouettes per size tier (about 8–12 shapes per tier, one texture atlas) is
   fine — visual uniqueness per rock is not required. This unblocks Option A.
2. **"Hundreds on screen" is a target, not an identified problem.** There is no
   specific reproduction (no particular late wave, horde mode, or custom field
   was observed). The stress scenario therefore represents the **target**: the
   game should comfortably handle hundreds of live asteroids, and we build the
   reproducible stress gym to stand in for the (currently hypothetical) real
   scenario.
3. **Schedule now, priority high.** The work item is already filed at `high`
   priority and is approved for planning/implementation.

## Acceptance criteria (final)

- AC1 — A reproducible asteroid stress scenario of at least ~200 live asteroids
  exists (new gym or documented launch setup) and is measurable with
  `npm run perf:measure`.
- AC2 — A same-host before/after measurement pair is recorded in
  `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`, with the measured asteroid counts reported (frame-time
  p50/p95 and the renderer/JS attribution).
- AC3 — Asteroids share a bounded set of baked silhouettes and render via a
  single texture (single batched draw call) rather than one unique texture or
  per-frame `Graphics` per rock.
- AC4 — `MAX_BAKED_ENEMY_BODY_TEXTURES` is no longer exhausted by an asteroid
  field (non-asteroid enemies keep their baked sprites under load).
- AC5 — Asteroid gameplay is unchanged: size tiers, speeds, rotation, split
  children, collision/hit radius, kill drops, and RNG-draw determinism all
  reproduce (determinism hashes from `node scripts/evaluate.mjs` unchanged).
- AC6 — Gym↔game parity holds: the shipped `PlayScene` and every asteroid-bearing
  gym run the same shared code path (`docs/GYM_PARITY.md` row + equivalence
  guard).
- AC7 — Visual parity is checked, not assumed (rock silhouette/rotation still
  read correctly; the shared-palette simplification is applied consistently
  across game and gyms).

## References

- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` — per-rock procedural body.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` (`_addStaticBodyLayer`) — bake seam.
- `src/utils/enemyBodyTextures.ts` — bounded per-silhouette texture cache (cap 64).
- `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` — unbounded per-wave asteroid count growth.
- `src/scenes/core/asteroidSplit.ts` — shared split helper.
- `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` — measurement rules, baked-texture precedent, budgets.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — gym↔game parity matrix.

# Fix Worklog schema drift (schemaVersion 8 vs 9) — audit-text persistence fails

## Problem statement

During the 2026-11-06 release run the ship audit gate's `wl update --audit-text`
failed with rc=1 while the AI_Hell worklog database was in a schema-drift state
(`schemaVersion=8` vs the tool's expected `9`), degrading audit fallback-notice
persistence: neither the assembled report nor the compact fallback notice could be
persisted, so the audit text field was effectively left unpersisted. The drift
self-perpetuates: three safe migrations are pending and `schemaVersion` only
advances to `9` when `wl doctor upgrade` runs and zero migrations remain pending.

## Users

- **Release producer** — "As the release producer, I want audit writes to succeed
  even when a worklog database is behind the current schema, so a schema-drift
  state can never silently break the release-gate audit persistence again."
- **Maintainer** — "As a maintainer, I want the drifted worklog roots brought to
  the current schema and verified, so the `schemaVersion=8 … expects 9` warning
  stops appearing on every `wl` invocation and pending migrations stop
  accumulating."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Audit-text write is drift-resilient (regression guard).** A test in the
   ContextHub `wl` suite proves that `wl update --audit-text` succeeds (rc=0)
   against a drifted-but-repairable worklog DB (e.g. `schemaVersion=8`, missing
   `audit_results.fingerprint` column), with the connect-time repair healing the
   missing column; the test fails against a build without the repair and passes
   with it.
2. **Verification evidence recorded.** `wl update --audit-text` — and the
   `wl audit-set` → `wl update --audit-text` sequence used by
   `persist_audit.py` — is exercised on the live AI_Hell DB and on a deliberately
   drifted sandbox DB copy; the rc=0 results (and any diagnostics) are recorded
   as a comment on this item before the AI_Hell upgrade is applied.
3. **AI_Hell drift resolved.** `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` on the AI_Hell
   worklog reports `pending: []` and no hook whose `status` is not `up-to-date`, and
   a plain `wl list --json` no longer prints the `schemaVersion=8 … expects 9`
   warning. The `--confirm` execution itself stays with *Run `wl doctor upgrade
   --confirm` in AI_Hell (AH-0MW1VJK63003KHD8)* (linked as related) — or, if this
   item's implementer performs it, the run and its before/after data-safety counts
   are recorded on both items. If the upgrade cannot be applied for any reason, the
   decision and its rationale must be recorded on this item (the "or decision
   recorded" clause).
4. **No audit-persistence regression next release.** The audit-skill persistence
   tests (`test_persist_audit_resilience.py` et al.) remain green and a
   release-path exercise (audit-set + audit-text persist) against a drifted DB
   copy succeeds end to end.
5. **Documentation and full suite.** All related documentation reflecting the
   drift-resilient audit persistence is updated (ContextHub
   `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md`, `src/migrations` comments, code comments as
   touched), and the full ContextHub `wl` test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Execution vehicle.** The `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` run against the AI_Hell
  production DB is the responsibility of *Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` in
  AI_Hell (AH-0MW1VJK63003KHD8)* (open, plan_complete, producer-approved). This
  item must not duplicate that run; it may operate on sandbox/verification DB
  copies only, and must not modify the production `.worklog/worklog.db` except
  through a co-ordinated execution recorded on both items.
- **Data safety.** `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` applies migrations inside one
  transaction with a pre-run backup (last 5 retained) and rolls the whole run back
  on any data-safety violation. The two historical `needsProducerReview` entries
  are neutralised no-ops; `20261102-drop-dependency-edge-target-fk` is safe but
  rebuilds the `dependency_edges` table (dropping the `toId` foreign key).
- **SQLite is the runtime source of truth.** Never edit
  `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` directly; use `wl` commands only; `wl sync` for
  transport.
- **Deterministic test only.** The ContextHub regression test must use a
  temp-DB fixture (the `createTempDir` pattern in `tests/migrations.test.ts`), no
  live `wl`/network/`pi` calls, and must drive the real `update --audit-text`
  path (store/CLI) that production uses so it cannot pass vacuously.
- **Cross-repo implementation.** The regression guard lands in ContextHub (the
  `wl` package); verification and co-ordination are recorded on this AI_Hell item.
  If an implementing session needs a tracker in ContextHub's worklog, a mirror
  child/sibling item may be created (`discovered-from:AH-0MW4W2CAJ000NUJZ`).

## Existing state

- AI_Hell DB: metadata `schemaVersion=8`; `audit_results.fingerprint` present
  (auto-repaired on connect); 3 pending safe migrations — two neutralised
  historical no-ops (`20260210-add-needsProducerReview`,
  `20261015-drop-needsProducerReview`) and one real
  (`20261102-drop-dependency-edge-target-fk`); 3 stale git hooks (pre-push,
  post-merge, post-rewrite).
- The current installed `wl` build auto-heals a drifted DB for audit writes:
  `wl update --audit-text` returned rc=0 against both the live AI_Hell DB and a
  deliberately fingerprint-stripped sandbox copy. The 2026-11-06 release failure
  is **not reproducible** with the current build.
- The warning will not clear on its own: `runMigrations` advances
  `metadata.schemaVersion` to `9` only when `computePending` is empty.

## Desired change

Stop schema drift from ever breaking audit-text persistence, and resolve the
outstanding drift:

1. Add the ContextHub regression guard (AC1) locking in the connect-time-repair
   behaviour for the audit write path.
2. Record verification evidence (AC2) on this item.
3. Bring the AI_Hell DB to schema 9 with the warning gone and pending `[]`
   (AC3), via the linked execution item or a recorded co-ordinated run.
4. Confirm the release/persist path works end to end and the relevant suites stay
   green (AC4–AC5).

## Key Files

- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/src/migrations/index.ts` — migration
  catalogue, `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION='9'`, connect-time required-column repair,
  schemaVersion advance logic; the behaviour the regression test locks in.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/tests/migrations.test.ts` — existing
  temp-DB migration tests; natural home for the drift-resilience regression test
  (or `tests/audit.test.ts`).
- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/src/commands/update.ts` — the
  `--audit-text` write path (`db.saveAuditResult`) that failed during the release.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/src/commands/audit.ts` — `wl audit-set`
  (audit_results) side of the persist sequence.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` — docs to update
  about drift-resilient behaviour.
- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — the
  ship-gate persist path that surfaced the failure (verification target).
- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/audit/tests/test_persist_audit_resilience.py`
  — existing persistence-resilience tests that must stay green.

## Related work

- **Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` in AI_Hell (AH-0MW1VJK63003KHD8)** — open,
  plan_complete, producer-approved; the AI_Hell execution vehicle (partial
  overlap; kept separate per producer decision, linked not merged).
- **Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` (WL-0MW1VJKO3009MHE0)** — ContextHub's own
  root's mirror item.
- **wl migrations: the audit-column drop can destroy unparseable legacy audit
  text; make the backfill lossless and gate the drop (WL-0MW1W61CG005K893)** —
  completed; the fix basis this item builds on (neutralised no-ops, schemaVersion
  advance on zero-pending, required-column repair).
- **Drop the dependency_edges.toId foreign key … (WL-0MVWABT2Z001XMSD D2)** —
  genesis of the one real pending migration `20261102-drop-dependency-edge-target-fk`.
- Audit skill persistence-resilience lineage (P8, SA-0MSF3RXUB000NLOI) and the

  degradation matters.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Race on the production DB.** Running `--confirm` in a live worklog store while
  other agents write risks transient inconsistency — mitigate with the tool's
  built-in backup + single-transaction rollback and the before/after data-safety
  counts; keep the run short.
- **Vacuous test.** A regression test that does not drive the real `update
  --audit-text` path could pass regardless of the repair — the test must exercise
  the store/CLI path used in production.
- **Scope creep.** Upgrading *every* drifted worklog root (ContextHub's own DB and
  other roots also print the warning) is a broader sweep — record as

- **Assumption — repair is intended.** The connect-time required-column repair is

- **Assumption — execution ownership.** This item's implementer performs the

- Q1 (scope): "What should this item actually deliver?" — Answer

  upgrade --confirm` on the drifted roots, verify `wl update --audit-text` works
